title: KS-528 gate 260 notes: a docs row is false on develop, two suite pins refuse legitimate shapes, and the checker misses two plants (gate 260)
description:
**BLUF:** Gate 260's notes on PR 2091 (KS-528, react-router 7 in the three portals, merged as `01b26bc772a7` on 2026-11-08 at 14:27:07Z): one false sentence in a shipped docs fragment (N1), two source-text pins in the router suite that refuse legitimate future code shapes (N3), and two planted defects that the suite's checker missed. None changes runtime behaviour. Low for all four, as Wednesday ruled (the PR 2091 addendum: "ticketed Low by the board seat after the merge"). One ticket, four items, because they come from one test pass.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate260-tier1-pr2091-r2/verdict.md`, round 2 of 2, GO WITH NOTES at head `e5742b73748b`. Evidence classes: the plants and the checker output were MEASURED by the gate; the line numbers below were READ ONLY by the board seat at develop `6c9a593df4ab`, which holds the merge. N2 of the same verdict (the wording "this PR's parent") was corrected in the PR body by the merge seat and in the KS-528 comment by an in-place edit, and is not an item here.

## Item 1 (N1, Nit): the cheat fragment's "cells" row says something false

`Projects Documents/fragments/cheat/KS-528-react-router-v7-portals.html`, line 12 at develop, says that against develop `b7d433fda83c` the checker reports R1 (23 files), R2 (6 lines), R3 (8 lines), R4 (2 rows) "and nothing for G1 to G6". MEASURED by the gate: it ran the head's checker on develop `abd044f6`, whose issuer has no opt-out, and got R0 x3, R1 x3, R2 x6, R3 x8, R4 x2 and G6 x1 (`G6 issuer: <BrowserRouter useTransitions={false}> is not present exactly once`). The flow fragment's "G1 to G5 are green on develop" is correct; only this row says G6. Fix shape (the gate's): "nothing for G1 to G5; G6 is red on develop by design".

## Item 2 (N3, Note, by design): two source-text pins refuse legitimate shapes

In `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/react_router_v7_portals.test.sh`: G6 (line 100) counts the single-line text `<BrowserRouter useTransitions={false}>`, and G3 (line 97) counts `<BrowserRouter[\s>]` in the issuer. MEASURED by the gate's plants: the opt-out reformatted over two lines turns G6 red, and a test wrapper under the issuer's `src` that renders a `<BrowserRouter>` turns G3 red. Neither is a defect today (G3 already refused the bare form in round 1, and the suite says to change a pin on purpose); the cost is that a harmless edit fails the suite until someone changes the pin.

## Item 3 (Low): an overrides key written `react-router-dom@6` is missed

MEASURED by the gate: a plant of the key `"react-router-dom@6"` in a manifest's `overrides` (npm accepts a `name@range` key) was not caught. Why Low: an actual install still lands in a lock file, and R3 scans the locks at any depth. READ ONLY: line 73 of the same suite tests the override keys for the exact name `react-router-dom` only.

## Item 4 (Nit): `bundleDependencies` is missed

MEASURED by the gate: a plant of `bundleDependencies: ["react-router-dom"]` was not caught. Why Nit: npm also requires a bundled dependency to be listed in `dependencies`, which R2 reads. READ ONLY: line 72 lists four dependency maps (`dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`) and not `bundleDependencies`.

Nothing here was run by the board seat; the gate's plants and measurements are as it reported them. The gate's own NOT TESTED list applies (Node 24, Docker, a live gateway, issuer vitest, the audit gates).

title: smoke-test.sh: auth-token skips are not counted so a run ends All checks passed; 127.0.0.1:6882 reads as remote (gate 243 N-2068)
description:
**BLUF:** Two residues of the smoke script after PR 2068 (KS-2080), both outside what that PR claims. (1) The skips PR 2068 counts are the direct-port and local-stack ones; the older "skipped (no auth token)" and "skipped (no admin token)" warnings still only warn, so a run that skipped those still closes with `All checks passed.` and exit 0. (2) "Local" means the exact string `http://localhost:6882`, so `http://127.0.0.1:6882`, a trailing slash or a slot 2 URL count as remote and skip sections 10 and 11 and the twelve direct-port checks. Both are Minor, READ ONLY, and fail loud or visible rather than silent. Low for each is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 105th, PR 2068 notes); filed as one ticket with two items, as she agreed.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, notes N-2068-1 and N-2068-2 on PR 2068 (KS-2080, merged as `6c9a593df4ab`). The fleet's shorthand is G243-N1 and G243-N2.

## Item 1 (N-2068-1): other skip warnings do not increment the skip count

READ ONLY (the gate, and the board seat at develop `6c9a593df4ab`). In `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh`, line 275 warns `GDPR endpoints — skipped (no auth token)` and line 402 warns `Platform API — skipped (no admin token)`; neither touches `SKIP` (the counter is declared at line 34 and incremented at lines 45 and 54). With `SKIP` at 0 the script reaches the branch at line 464 that prints `All checks passed.` and exits 0. PR 2068's claim covers only the direct-port and local-stack skips, so this is outside its claim, but the new closing sentence is still reachable with a skip printed above it. Fix shape (the owner's call, READ ONLY): count those two skips in `SKIP` or word the closing line to mention skipped checks of any kind.

## Item 2 (N-2068-2): "local" is one exact string

READ ONLY. Line 24 is `[ "$GATEWAY" = "http://localhost:6882" ] || DIRECT_PORTS=no`. Any other spelling of the same stack (`http://127.0.0.1:6882`, a trailing slash) sets `DIRECT_PORTS=no`, so sections 10 and 11 and the twelve direct-port checks are skipped on a genuinely local stack. The warning text says so and the exit stays 0, so it is visible. For a slot 2 URL the skip is arguably right (sections 10 and 11 name slot 1's containers). Fix shape (the owner's call, READ ONLY): normalise the host before the comparison, or state in the warning that only the exact default counts as local.

The gate found nothing that parses `All checks passed.`: `git grep` finds only the suite itself, and the Makefile and the package manifest call the script without parsing it (READ ONLY, the gate's read).

No run against a box and no full green run of the script (the gate had no stack; PR 2068's READY says the same).

title: systemTest format gate: the line-730 selection pipe may close early on GNU grep and select no package on a large push (gate 247 F74-1)
description:
**BLUF:** `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh` line 730 selects packages with `printf '%s\n' "$changed_paths" | grep "^systemTest/${p}/" > /dev/null`. On the macOS host that works. Gate 247 recalls that GNU grep treats output to `/dev/null` like `-q` and stops at the first match. If so, on Linux the pipe closes early, the pipeline returns 141 under `pipefail`, the package reads as not selected, and the gate exits 0 at line 739 without a word. The GNU premise is the gate's memory and is UNMEASURED. First step: measure the line-730 form on Linux with GNU grep. Medium is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 104th, PR 2074 notes).

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate247-tier1-tests-tooling/verdict.md`, finding F74-1 (Major, conditional) on PR 2074 (KS-1728 batch 2, merged as `15dca468b86f`). The gate says it is not a reason to hold that PR. The verdict's label is F74-1; the fleet's shorthand "G247-F1" names this finding and also PR 2069's F69-1, so this ticket uses the verdict's label.

## Evidence

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by the gate (macOS, `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD, the only grep on that host): a wrapper `grep` on PATH that adds `-q` only when stdout is `/dev/null`. With a 1.1 MB changed list, real grep gives exit 1, REFUSED, 3 of 3; the wrapper gives exit 0 with no refusal, 3 of 3; a one-path control gives exit 1, REFUSED. So if a grep behaves like the wrapper, the gate goes silently green.
* UNMEASURED: that GNU grep behaves like the wrapper. No GNU grep was available to the gate.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`): line 730 is as quoted; lines 737 to 740 take `selected` empty to `exit 0` with the comment "nothing under a gated package — say nothing, cost nothing". `.githooks/pre-push` lines 375 to 380 speak of Linux and dash, so the hook contemplates Linux pushers.
* The failure needs a grep that stops early and a changed list larger than the pipe buffer. The gate rates the likelihood low on today's macOS pushers, where it does not occur (measured).
* The census behind KS-1728 cannot find this form, because its regex looks for `-q`.

## History

KS-1716 (Done) proposed this exact form as the "read to EOF" fix for the original `grep -q` loss and measured it (3 of 3 runs selected all five packages); the ticket names a 64 KiB macOS pipe buffer and never mentions GNU grep. PR 2074 converted twelve other product lines to the same form. The same measurement also settles F74-2 (the statement "grep reads to EOF" stated without its condition), which Wednesday recorded on the PR without a ticket.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

After the measurement: if GNU grep stops early, select without a writer process (a pure-bash `case` match on the list, as KS-1716 notes PS-1254 did) and add a cell over a path list larger than the pipe buffer on a platform that stops early. If GNU grep reads to EOF, record the measurement here and close.

title: pre-push hook: a failing git diff reads as no change and the hook exits 0 before leg 1, so a RED commit pushes (gate 263 G1)
description:
**BLUF:** The real pre-push hook treats a failing `git diff` as an empty change set. With `git config diff.orderFile` naming a missing file, `git diff` exits 128 with no output, the changed set stays empty, and the hook exits 0 before leg 1: a RED commit pushes with rc 0 and no preflight line. Gate 263 measured this on the hook fixture at `35bcfa000`; the same lines are on develop `6c9a593df4ab`. High is Wednesday's call.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate263-tier1-x8-prerun-driver-r3/verdict.md`, finding G1 (a note outside the tool under test, which the gate calls the most important thing it found). Not a PR-merge item: it waits on no PR. A build seat fixes the hook; this ticket only records it.

## What was measured, and what was only read

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 263 (scratch worlds, local bare origins): `git config diff.orderFile <missing file>` makes `git diff` exit 128 with empty output, while `status`, `rev-parse` and `merge-base` still exit 0. The gate probed 17 `diff.*` and `core.*` faults and found this one shape. The real hook fixture, called directly with a new-branch stdin line on a RED commit: with the fault, rc 0 and "Blockchain/Dev changes detected" is never printed; without the fault, rc 1, the preflight ran and failed. Evidence in the gate folder: `evidence/order.out`, produced by `evidence/g263_order.py`.
* On the same fault the pre-run tool (X 8th's) still runs the preflight, so the pre-run path is stronger than the hook here.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`; I did not run the hook): in `.githooks/pre-push`, lines 129, 143 and 252 end `|| true` after `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only ...`. Line 251 sets `_informative=1` before the diff at line 252, so the KS-882 branch at line 271 (every base contains HEAD, run unconditionally) does not fire. With `changed` empty, line 372 `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` returns success before the preflight message at line 374. These are the lines the gate cited at `35bcfa000`; the gate's fixture hook is not necessarily develop's current hook, and the lines match.

## Why it is the same class as two fixed holes

The hook's own comments record KS-854 (lines 156 to 160: an unresolvable base left `changed` empty and the hook returned success before leg 1) and KS-882 (lines 181 to 187, banner at line 272: a base equal to HEAD gave an empty diff and the same exit). Both fixes treat "cannot compute" as "run the preflight" (lines 276 to 277 and 284 to 285 set `changed` to an unconditional marker and `st_all=1`). A diff that fails is the same case: an uncomputable change set is not a clean one.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

Capture the diff's exit status at lines 129, 143 and 252 instead of discarding it with `|| true`; on a non-zero status take the KS-854 and KS-882 path (banner, unconditional marker, `st_all=1`). Regression test: in a scratch repo set `diff.orderFile` to a missing path, push a RED commit, expect rc 1 and the "changes detected" line; the same push without the fault expects the same result.

## Related, not this defect

* KS-1483 (Backlog): the hook diffs HEAD, not the pushed ref. A different cause, same symptom class.
* KS-2091 (Backlog): no hook suite proves that a red preflight makes the hook refuse a push.
* KS-989, KS-1063, KS-1482 (Done): earlier holes in the same hook.
* Gate 263's G2 (the pre-run's own copy of the changed set, Minor) and G3 (clean means clean to `git status`) concern the pre-run tool and are not filed here.

title: auth: a PATCH on an OAuth app with no scopes skips the privileged-scope check, so an app that stores admin:read or admin:write keeps it
description:
**BLUF:** On `PATCH /api/oauth/apps/{id}`, the privileged-scope check runs only on the `scopes` in the request body. A PATCH without `scopes` skips it and leaves the app's stored scopes as they are, so an app that already stores `admin:read` or `admin:write` keeps it, whoever the caller is and whatever other fields the PATCH changes. PR 2061 (KS-1536 3b, merged as `092d30706b95`) described the loss for a bare `admin` token as "cannot register or keep" those scopes. The register half holds; "keep" is not enforced. The wording is already corrected in place (KS-1536 comment `dec43279`); this ticket records the behaviour behind it.

Source: gate 244 (KS-1536, PR 2061 section), finding F7 (recorded as G244-F7): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate244-tier1-ks1536/verdict.md`. Every line below I read myself at develop `092d30706b9561bb7d28aeffedf1e37ba62b4cd5`, the merge of PR 2061.

1. The check. `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts` lines 1245 to 1250: `OAUTH_PRIVILEGED_SCOPES` is `admin:read` and `admin:write`, and `privilegedScopesIn(scopes)` returns the privileged ones among the scopes it is given, or none for no scopes. In the PATCH handler (line 1397), line 1412 splits `scopes` from the rest of the body, line 1413 builds `updates` with `allowedScopes` only when `scopes !== undefined`, and lines 1421 to 1424 refuse with 403 only when `privilegedScopesIn(scopes)` is not empty and the caller is not a platform admin.
2. What follows. A PATCH with no `scopes` gives `privilegedScopesIn(undefined)` an empty result, so the 403 never fires, and `updates` carries no `allowedScopes`, so the stored scopes are untouched. Evidence class: READ ONLY (the gate's and mine); no request was sent.
3. Who holds such an app. UNMEASURED. The gate looked for no app that stores a privileged scope, and neither did I.

The gate gives no fix shape. Whether keeping a stored privileged scope is intended is the owner's question; this ticket only records that "keep" is not enforced, which the corrected comment on KS-1536 now says.

Not claimed: no run by me, no request, no database read.

Related: KS-1536 (the parent; comment `dec43279` was edited in place on 2026-11-08 to say this) and KS-1846 (scope vocabulary and enforcement drift, a different gap; read whole, no mention of PATCH).

title: api-gateway: admin-minted connector keys share the identity connector:api-key, so one tenant's key can list and delete another's inbox rows
description:
**BLUF:** Admin-minted API keys carry no connector id, so the gateway gives every one of them the same `userId`, `connector:api-key`. Gate 246 measured that tenant B's key can then list, and delete, a notification row that tenant A's key placed in that inbox. PR 2072 (KS-1448, merged as `7eda23b34d3b`) now refuses a `userId` other than the caller's, with a connector key allowed its own id; for this population "its own id" is the shared one, so that ruling does not close it. The identity sharing predates PR 2072, which narrows the route. High is Wednesday's call.

Source: gate 246 (PR 2072, KS-1448), finding 72-1, recorded by Wednesday as G246-F1: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate246-tier1-services/verdict.md`, and her note `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/fleet/briefs_staged/2026-11-08_B99_answer_notes_2072.md`. 1. Where the identity comes from. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` line 572 builds `userId: connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}`, and line 312 sets `connectorId: data.connectorId || ''`. The comment at lines 52 to 55 of the same file says `connectorId` is null for admin-minted keys, so every such key gets the one userId `connector:api-key`: "one bucket across all tenants".
2. What PR 2072 ruled. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` lines 315 to 327: `if (userId !== getUserId(req))` answers 403 for every principal, and a connector key may create for its own id. For a key with no connector id, its own id is `connector:api-key`, the same string for every such key of every tenant. Neither the PR nor its ticket comment says so.
3. The steps. Evidence class: MEASURED at runtime by gate 246, for the route through the real `authenticateToken` with the security service's answer stubbed to `connectorId: null`. (1) Key A, of tenant A, posted `type: security` with an `actionUrl` to `connector:api-key`: 201. (2) Key B, of tenant B, listed the row: 200. (3) Key B deleted it: 200. (4) Key A posting to `victim`: 403, so PR 2072's rule holds for every other id.
4. Not measured. Whether admin-minted keys exist on any live box, and whether anyone reads such an inbox. The gate notes that connector inboxes are unlikely to have human readers.

Shared root: every API key without a connector id is the one principal `connector:api-key`. KS-1685 records that for vc-issuer and says cross-tenant stays separated there; the notification routes act on that string with no tenant check, as measured above, so here it does not. The transfer service's `GET /api/notifications` has the same root: KS-2119.

Fix shapes, the gate's: refuse admin-minted keys on this route, or derive a per-key id; at minimum, name the gap, which this ticket does. The regression test to add: two keys with null `connectorId` cannot see each other's rows.

Not claimed: no run by me, and no reading of any live box.

title: transfer: a transfer row opened by a key that names no real users has no exit, and nothing expires it
description:
**BLUF:** A transfer row that a key opened, and whose two named parties are not real users, has no exit. Approve, reject and execute read 404 for everyone, cancel belongs to the initiator (the key), and PR 2077 refuses a key before that is checked. The row stays `pending_approval` and nothing expires it. PR 2077 (KS-2081, merged as `765701307eb3`) stops keys opening new rows, so this concerns rows that already exist. Whether any exist is not measured.

Source: gate 240 (PR 2077, KS-2081), finding F2, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate240-tier1-pr2077-ks2081/verdict.md`. Every line number below I read myself at develop `7eda23b34d3b7a413ca8f9c0945c7843708ce9f4`, which holds the merge; they match the gate's.

Why there is no exit. `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` lines 377 and 378 check only that `currentOwnerId` and `newOwnerId` are GUID-shaped (`z.string().guid()`), not that a user holds them. `decideTransferAccess` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/transferAccess.ts` (lines 82 to 88) answers 404 to anyone the row does not name, and reads no role (its comment, line 79, says so). Its cancel table (lines 54 to 59) lets only `initiatedBy` cancel, and on a key-opened row that is the key's principal. So "its parties can still reject" holds only if the parties exist. A person-opened row keeps the initiator's cancel as an exit; a key-opened row loses it.
2. No expiry. A search of `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` at develop for `setInterval`, `cron` or `expire` finds 0 matches (the control, `createNotification`, finds 8).
3. The measurement. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 240, cell O6. A row was warmed through `loadFromDb` with two random GUID parties. A SYSTEM_ADMIN read approve, reject, execute and cancel as 404, 404, 404, 404; a key read cancel as 403; the status stayed `pending_approval`.

The gate's question Q4 gives a read-only query for someone commissioned to run it on each box: count `svc_transfers` rows whose `initiated_by` is not a canonical UUID, grouped by status, then check the pending ones' owner ids against `users.id`. `initiated_by` is TEXT in all three schemas, so key-opened rows do persist. I ran nothing against any box.

The gate names no fix shape for F2. If the count is 0, nothing is needed beyond this record. If it is not 0, an exit for such rows (an expiry, or an administrator's cancel) is the owner's decision, and an administrator's cancel would reverse the "no role is read" rule that `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/transferAccess.ts` states at line 79.

title: Connector-key rotate answers rotated true with no warning while an older organisation key with no connector id still validates
description:
**BLUF:** The connector-key rotate (register-connector with rotate on) answers `rotated: true`, a count of 1 and no warning while an older key of the same organisation, one that carries no connector id, still validates. It happens on the retry after a count of 0, and also on the first call when the organisation holds both kinds of key, so no 0 is needed. The cause is in security's retire, which matches only the connector id; the gateway cannot see the older key. Gate 257 measured it on real PostgreSQL. It is old behaviour that PR 2073 narrows (the 0 itself is now honest) and does not remove. Priority High is Wednesday's call; the gate graded the finding Medium. Wednesday's ruling on the fix direction, under Kam's card `secuura-ks-1152-rotate-says-rotated-when-old-key-lives-1106` = b ("Keep rotating, but answer 'rotated: false' and say why", ruled 2026-11-06 15:00:34 AEDT, read with `tools/decision_queue.sh show`): the fix extends that honest answer to these keys; it does NOT retire them.

Source: gate 257, tier 1, round 2 of 2, PR 2073 (KS-1152 R-880-1), finding F1 and the section "For Kam, at the top", `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate257-tier1-pr2073-r2/verdict.md`, lines 17 to 34 and 40 to 49. 1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 257 on real PostgreSQL 15 (the gate's own cluster), through a real gateway route over real security, at PR 2073's head `2684a29d8f576ff74634f07ad6576af5bd00370b` and again on the develop merge.
   * G2a, the first call with a count of 0: 200, `rotated` false, `priorKeysRevoked` 0, `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`. The older key and the new key both validate.
   * G2b, the retry: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the key the 0 call returned is no longer valid.
   * G3, an organisation that holds both an older key with no connector id and a key with the connector id, first call: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the connector key is retired.
2. Where. Evidence class: READ. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` at PR 2073's head, line 979: `rotated: rotate && existing.rows.length > 0 && priorKeysRetired && priorKeysRevoked >= 1`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` at develop `abd044f63a9dd5673f1b9ff7a2b1e42e1c26de82` (the file is not changed by PR 2073), lines 239 and 246: both retire statements end `WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true`, so a key with no connector id is never matched.

4. The fix direction. Ruled by Wednesday (ADDENDUM 11:39:30Z): extend the honest answer, `rotated: false` with a reason, to these keys; do not retire them. The gate's two fix shapes were that security reports how many active keys of the organisation remain after the retire, or that the retire also takes the organisation's keys that have no connector id. The first fits the ruling; the second is what the ruling excludes. A regression test the owner should add (the gate): G3's shape, asserting that `rotated` is not true while the older key validates. If this behaviour stays for now, the gate asks for one sentence each in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` and in the spec: "`rotated: true` says nothing about an older key with no connector id; a retry after a 0 answers `rotated: true` with that key still active."

By the gate: rotation is platform-admin only (its GUARDRAIL 1), so a K admin reads the reply; whether Platform S reads `rotated` is unknown; the only code reader is systemTest, which stops at `rotated: true`. The contract Stuart's team reads says a retry does not help but not that the retry answers `rotated: true`, and it does not mention G3.

description:
**BLUF:** If the stored platform-settings document holds a category named `__proto__`, the admin Settings page's save grouping writes that category's fields onto `Object.prototype` in the admin's browser. Gate 256 measured it on both, and by its model any admin caller of the settings PUT can store such a key. It found no gadget and looked for none. 1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by the gate (tsx; the head module against develop's grouping logic copied out). It planted the wire document `{"settings":{"general":{...},"__proto__":{"g256polluted":"yes"}}}` (the contents of `general` are elided as in the verdict); `JSON.parse` makes `__proto__` an own key. A control read before each run gave `({}).g256polluted` as undefined. After one save build it was `"yes"` at both the head and develop. The save request body itself did not carry the key.
2. The line on develop. Evidence class: READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` lines 63 to 71 group the form values by category: `if (!updates[category]) { updates[category] = {}; }` (lines 67 to 69), then `updates[category][field] = formValues[key];` (line 70). For the name `__proto__`, `updates[category]` is not empty (it is the object prototype), so the branch is skipped and line 70 assigns onto `Object.prototype`. That last step is my reading of the two lines; the gate's run is what measured it.
3. The line at PR 2058's head. Evidence class: READ at `527d67b1852e`. `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/lib/settingsSavePayload.ts` line 84 is `const target = (updates[category] ??= {}) as Settings;` and line 85 assigns `target[field] = value`. That file exists only on the PR's head (it is absent from develop at `cfb6c1573ba9`); the same reading applies, because `??=` keeps a value that is not null or undefined.
4. Whether such a key can be stored. Evidence class: MEASURED by the gate on a model of the gateway's spread (it keeps an own `__proto__` key), plus READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`, the PUT validates only `integrations[].config.allowedDocumentTypes` (lines 1169 to 1179) and line 1200 is the merge `{ ...PLATFORM_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, ...existing, ...body }`; I found no check on category names between line 1164 and line 1200.
